title: Wavelet rollout minimap + release digest (May 2027) - draft
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact rollout minimap for the 'wavelet' deployment pattern: several short, targeted ramps across customer cohorts to validate perf, correctness, and cost signals while minimizing blast radius. This doc bundles the calendar, the preflight and canary checklists, signal thresholds, and the draft release digest template we’ll publish after the run.

Goals:
- Validate runtime kernel selection changes and a new batching heuristic under representative traffic.
- Keep 99th percentile latency within 20% of baseline across target models.
- Detect quality regressions on the focal prompt set within 24h.
- Limit cost delta to +10% for dedicated capacity customers during the window.

High-level schedule (minimap):
- May 18: Preflight dry-run (internal only). Smoke + load generator from staging->canary.
- May 19: Night pilot (2% traffic) for internal beta orgs (09:00–18:00 UTC).
- May 20: Canary A (5% production traffic) – hold 3h, evaluate metrics, then 12h watch.
- May 21–24: Wavelet ramp (A/B micro-ramps) 5% -> 25% -> 50% (24h between ramps).
- May 25: Full lift to 100% or rollback decision by 14:00 UTC.
- May 26–28: Post-release monitoring & digest prep.

Preflight checklist (owner: Aisha):
- [ ] Build: confirm CI artifacts (sha + churn summary) match release note. Link: PR 1428.
- [ ] Infra: GPU pool sizing for bursts; verify reserved capacity quotas.
- [ ] Config: rollout policy pinned in orchestration config and annotated with ticket id.
- [ ] Safety lanes: emergency throttle and safety-lane runbook attached to the incident pager.
- [ ] Observability: dashboards (latency, error-rate, token-cost) copied and baseline snapshot captured.
- [ ] Eval: run focal prompt set (50k tokens) against candidate and baseline; attach diff summary.
- [ ] Communications: calendar invites set, stakeholder Slack channel created (#release-wavelet-2027-05).

Canary & ramp guardrails (on-deck SRE + release lead):
- Hard stop if 99th latency > baseline * 1.5 for >5 minutes.
- Hard stop if error rate > 0.5% sustained for 10 minutes.
- Quality flag: regression on focal prompt set with statistically significant drop in exact-match or curated quality metric -> immediate pause.
- Cost flag: sustained per-token cost > baseline + 15% for 4h -> investigate and consider throttle.

Observability signals (primary):
- latency.p50/p95/p99 per model and per-route
- infra.gpu_utilization and queue_depth by pool
- errors.rate and error_types (OOM, timeout, decode_error)
- quality.eval_delta.focal_prompt_set (automated eval job)
- billing.per_token and per-req cost trend
- user-facing latency SLO breaches (error budget burn)

Communication & incident flow:
- Channel: #release-wavelet-2027-05 (Slack).
- Paging policy: on-call SRE -> escalation to Release Lead (Aisha) -> Eng Manager -> Product PM.
- Daily sync times while active: 09:30 UTC readiness, 15:30 UTC mid-run, 19:30 UTC end-of-day quick debrief (only if active ramp).

Rollback decision tree (quick):
- If safety guard triggers, move to partial rollback to previous model variant and scale down traffic to 0% over 10 minutes.
- If multiple independent failures across regions, initiate full rollback and declare incident.
- Document all decisions in the release ticket and tag stakeholders.

Post-release digest (draft template):
Title: Wavelet rollout — May 2027 — Release digest
Summary: short one-paragraph description of what changed and why.
What we measured: bullets of key metrics (p50/p95/p99 changes, error-rate, cost delta, quality delta on focal set).
Actions taken: rollouts, mitigations, or follow-ups.
Outstanding work: tickets to track regressions or optimizations.
Lessons & next steps: quick items for runoff (tuning kernel selection, batching window).
Links: CI build, PRs, dashboards, incident ticket if any.
Owner for digest: Marta Silva (prep), Release Lead: Aisha Kapoor (publish).

Postmortem anchors (if incident):
- Timeline + decision log (every handoff timestamped).
- Root cause hypothesis and evidence.
- Mitigations and follow-ups with owners and due dates.

Notes + open questions:
- We should trial a 'quality-sampling' lane that routes 0.5% of requests to candidate for deeper offline eval without affecting production traffic; TBD infra cost.
- Consider adding a short TTL to KV cache warming to reduce blast when rolling kernel behavior.

Quick links:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1428
- Eval job run: https://ci.redwood.ai/job/eval/2027-05-11
- Dashboards: production/rollout/wavelet-2027-05

If you’re reading this and own any checklist item above, add a short status line under your name in this doc and tag @Aisha. This remains a working doc until the digest is published.
